description:
Get the downloadable print templates and design guides for a Smartpress product. Returns:

- **summary**: a one-line description of what this product has — paraphrase this rather than counting the arrays yourself.
- **designGuides**: instructional PDFs about how to set artwork up (bleed, folding). Not tied to a size.
- **templateGroups**: the print templates, in the groups the layout team defined (e.g. "Flat", "Single Fold"). `group` is omitted when a product's templates are not grouped, which is common.
- Each entry has a **label** (what to call it to the customer) and **files** (format -> download URL, e.g. `{"pdf": "https://...", "idml": "https://..."}`).

Use this when a customer asks for a template, a layout guide, artwork setup help, dimensions to design to, or an InDesign file. If you only know the product by name, call find_products first and pass its "id" (e.g. "SLS_7") here.

Rules:
- Give customers the exact URLs this tool returned. Never construct, guess, or edit a template URL.
- Use the **label** verbatim when naming a template. Labels are display text written by the layout team — do NOT parse them as dimensions or assume a label matches the customer's configured size.
- Only offer a format that appears in that entry's **files**. Most templates have PDF and InDesign, but some have only one, and a few are Illustrator or spreadsheets.
- If a product has none, say so plainly. Many products have no templates yet — that is normal, not an error, and you must not substitute another product's template.

format.description: Only return templates available in this format, and only that file. Omit for all formats.

include.description: Limit the response to print templates or to design guides. Omit for both.

productId.description: Product ID with prefix, e.g. "SLS_7". Get it from find_products or the page context.

name: get_product_templates
